backup.title: Backup
backup.intro: A backup is one file with your library data folder (notes, highlights, citations, projects, taxonomy), and optionally your chat history and reading state. Your original documents are not included: they stay where they are. API keys and tokens are never saved.
backup.internalNote: This is your own copy, in a folder you choose, that you can move, verify and restore. It is separate from the automatic safety copy the app keeps for itself to undo its own mistakes.

destination.label: Destination folder
destination.hint: Choose a folder outside your library folders, for example on another disk or a synced folder.
destination.syncNote: If the destination is in a synced folder, the backup files are uploaded with it. Automatic backups never include chat history; manual ones only if you choose it below.
destination.pick: Choose where to save the backups

schedule.label: How often
schedule.hint: Checked once when the app starts; nothing runs in the background.

backup.lastNone: No backup of this library found in the destination yet.
backup.stale: The last backup is {{days}} days old (more than {{limit}}). Consider making a new one.

includeLocal.label: Include chat history, usage counters and reading state
includeLocal.hint: Data that cannot be rebuilt. Search index, caches and thumbnails are never saved: they are rebuilt after a restore.

restore.title: Restore a backup
restore.intro: The backup becomes a new library. Nothing that exists now is overwritten, and your documents are not copied or changed.
restore.rootHint: Choose an empty folder: the restore creates a new library there. The data folder is created inside it.
restore.chooseRootTitle: Choose the folder of the documents
restore.name: Name of the library
restore.nameHint: Leave empty to keep the name from the backup.
restore.local: Restore chat history, usage counters and reading state
restore.settingsHint: Replaces language, profile, appearance, shortcuts and guide state with those of the backup.
restore.settingsMissing: The settings were not saved in this backup.
restore.cancelled: Cancelled. No library and no data folder were left behind.
restore.secretsTitle: Enter these again in the settings (secrets are never stored in a backup):
restore.secretsHint: Open the settings: the AI and MCP sections.
restore.secretsNone: No secrets need to be entered again.
restore.rebuilding: The first search may take a little longer while the index is rebuilt.
restore.resetTitle: Some settings were switched to safe values because they came from a backup:
restore.resetHint: Turn them on again in the settings if you want them (MCP and AI sections).

reset.confirm-before-send: Asking before sending text to Claude is on.

restore.libraryRoot: This folder is already a library. Choose an empty folder: the restore creates a new library.
restore.manageHint: To remove a library you no longer want from the list:

backup.notListed: This file is not in the backup folder

options.title: Options
options.keepHelp: It applies when the automatic backup is on. Older automatic backups are removed; backups you make by hand are never removed.

maintenance.title: Maintenance and performance
maintenance.intro: Sizes of what the app keeps for the active library, and tools to free space. Nothing here touches your documents or your notes.
maintenance.memoryValue: {{rss}} MB in use, {{heap}} MB of script data

clean.title: Free space
clean.hint: Deletes only data the app can rebuild by itself (it is recomputed when needed). The library data folder, the search index, chats and settings are never touched.

maintenance.busy: The app is busy with a scan, a network build or a backup. Try again when it has finished.

support.title: Support
support.hint: The diagnostics text lists versions, language, counts and sizes. It never contains file names, document titles, paths, keys or tokens.

maintenance.backupsNote: The app's own safety copy (the one that undoes its mistakes) is not touched by cleaning; it is cleaned by the app itself.
maintenance.limits: Background workers stop after 30 s without work. The limits of the app are fixed: here they can only be read.
